questions.name: State and Local Governments
questions.keyword: Government-wide financial statements — GASB reporting model, statement of net position (governmental/business-type activities columns), statement of activities (program revenues, general revenues, net position changes)
questions.text: Under GASB Statement No. 34, what is the measurement focus and basis of accounting used in government-wide financial statements?

answers.text: Full accrual basis with an economic resources measurement focus — recognizing all assets, deferred outflows, liabilities, and deferred inflows regardless of when cash flows occur
Modified accrual basis with a current financial resources measurement focus — the same as governmental fund financial statements
Cash basis — government-wide statements measure only actual cash receipts and disbursements
The basis varies by activity — governmental activities use modified accrual; business-type activities use full accrual

explanations.a: GASB Statement No. 34 established the dual-reporting model: Government-wide financial statements: Full accrual basis / Economic resources measurement focus — long-term assets (capital assets, infrastructure), long-term liabilities (bonds payable, pension obligations), deferred outflows/inflows are all recognized; revenues are recognized when earned (not when received); expenses are recognized when incurred (not when paid). Governmental fund financial statements: Modified accrual basis / Current financial resources measurement focus — only short-term financial resources are recognized; revenues recognized when measurable and available; expenditures recognized when incurred if current liability; long-term assets and liabilities are NOT reported in funds.
explanations.b: Modified accrual with current financial resources measurement focus is used for GOVERNMENTAL FUND financial statements — not government-wide financial statements. This is a key distinction in governmental accounting: fund statements and government-wide statements use different bases of accounting.
explanations.c: Cash basis is not an acceptable basis for GAAP financial reporting by state and local governments. Government-wide statements use full accrual, and fund statements use modified accrual.
explanations.d: Both the governmental activities column and the business-type activities column in government-wide financial statements use the SAME basis — full accrual with economic resources measurement focus. The distinction between governmental and business-type activities is about the type of activity, not the accounting basis.

questions.name: State and Local Governments
questions.keyword: Government-wide financial statements — GASB reporting model, statement of net position (governmental/business-type activities columns), statement of activities (program revenues, general revenues, net position changes)
questions.text: A city's statement of activities shows the following for the Public Safety function: program expenses $4,200,000; charges for services $800,000; operating grants $600,000. Property tax revenues (general) are $15,000,000. Calculate the net expense/(revenue) of the Public Safety function and explain how it is presented in the statement of activities.

answers.text: Net expense = $4,200,000 — all program expenses are presented as a single line without netting program revenues

Net expense = $2,800,000 ($4,200,000 − $800,000 − $600,000); presented as the function's net burden on general revenues; property taxes are shown separately as general revenues that offset the net expenses of all functions combined
Net expense = $2,800,000 ($4,200,000 − $800,000 − $600,000); the property taxes reduce the net expense because they are general revenues
Net revenue = $11,400,000 (property taxes $15,000,000 minus public safety net expense $3,600,000)

explanations.a: Program revenues (charges for services and grants directly related to the function) are netted against program expenses in the statement of activities — the net expense or net revenue is the key figure presented for each function. Showing all program expenses without netting would overstate the burden on general revenues.
explanations.b: Statement of activities format under GASB 34: Program revenues: Charges for services: $800,000 + Operating grants: $600,000 = $1,400,000 total program revenues. Net expense of Public Safety = Program expenses ($4,200,000) − Program revenues ($1,400,000) = $2,800,000 net expense. This $2,800,000 represents the cost of public safety services NOT covered by program revenues — the net burden on the general taxpayer. Property taxes ($15,000,000) are GENERAL REVENUES presented separately below the functional expense table. They are not allocated to specific functions. The statement structure: Functions listed with net expense/(revenue) for each → total net expense → then general revenues (property taxes, sales taxes, unrestricted grants) → change in net position. This format shows citizens how much each program costs after considering its own revenues.
explanations.c: This calculation is correct ($2,800,000 net expense) but incorrectly characterizes property taxes as reducing the function's net expense. Property taxes are GENERAL REVENUES — they benefit the government as a whole, not a specific function, and are presented below the functional net expense totals.
explanations.d: Netting property taxes against public safety expenses would combine function-specific and general revenues — violating the statement of activities format that separates program revenues (function-specific) from general revenues (entity-wide).

questions.name: State and Local Governments
questions.keyword: Government-wide financial statements — GASB reporting model, statement of net position (governmental/business-type activities columns), statement of activities (program revenues, general revenues, net position changes)
questions.text: A city's statement of net position shows: capital assets (net of depreciation) $45,000,000; other assets $12,000,000; related debt on capital assets $30,000,000; other liabilities $5,000,000. Net position of $22,000,000 is classified into three components. Calculate each component of net position assuming: restricted net position $3,000,000 (for special purposes); remaining net position is unrestricted.

answers.text: Net investment in capital assets: $45,000,000; Restricted: $3,000,000; Unrestricted: ($26,000,000); Total: $22,000,000
Net investment in capital assets: $15,000,000; Restricted: $3,000,000; Unrestricted: $4,000,000 — total confirms to $22,000,000
Net investment in capital assets: $15,000,000; Restricted: $3,000,000; Unrestricted: $4,000,000; Total: $22,000,000
All net position is reported as a single unrestricted amount — component classification is optional

explanations.a: Net investment in capital assets should be the net amount (capital assets minus related debt), not the gross capital asset amount. Using $45,000,000 (gross) and showing negative unrestricted net position misrepresents the components.
explanations.b: Same correct result as option A but presented with less completeness. Both A and C have the right numbers; A is more explicit about the derivation.
explanations.c: Net position component calculation (GASB 34): (1) Net investment in capital assets = Capital assets (net of accumulated depreciation) − Related outstanding debt + Related deferred outflows of resources − Related deferred inflows of resources = $45,000,000 − $30,000,000 = $15,000,000. (2) Restricted = Net position subject to externally imposed constraints (by creditors, grantors, laws, regulations) = $3,000,000 (given). (3) Unrestricted = Total net position − Net investment in capital assets − Restricted = $22,000,000 − $15,000,000 − $3,000,000 = $4,000,000. Verification: Total assets = $45,000,000 + $12,000,000 = $57,000,000. Total liabilities = $30,000,000 + $5,000,000 = $35,000,000. Net position = $57,000,000 − $35,000,000 = $22,000,000. ✓ The three components must sum to total net position.
explanations.d: GASB 34 paragraph 34 specifically requires separate display of the three components of net position — net investment in capital assets, restricted, and unrestricted. This disaggregation is mandatory, not optional, and provides important information about the nature and availability of net position.

questions.name: State and Local Governments
questions.keyword: Government-wide financial statements — GASB reporting model, statement of net position (governmental/business-type activities columns), statement of activities (program revenues, general revenues, net position changes)
questions.text: A city operates a water utility as a proprietary (enterprise) fund and maintains governmental activities for general operations. The water utility earns $3,000,000 in customer charges and incurs $2,200,000 in operating expenses and $400,000 in depreciation. General government property tax revenues are $8,000,000 and general expenses are $7,500,000. Prepare the government-wide statement of activities analysis showing change in net position for each activity type.

answers.text: Only the governmental activities are included in government-wide statements — proprietary funds are excluded
Governmental activities: deficit of $7,500,000; Business-type activities: surplus of $3,000,000; difference is not meaningful
Business-type activities profit: $800,000 ($3,000,000 − $2,200,000); depreciation is not an expense in government accounting

Governmental activities: change in net position $500,000 (revenues $8M − expenses $7.5M); Business-type activities: change in net position $400,000 ($3M − $2.2M − $0.4M); Total government-wide change: $900,000

explanations.a: GASB 34 requires that BOTH governmental activities AND business-type activities be presented in government-wide financial statements. Enterprise funds (proprietary funds) provide the basis for business-type activities reporting in the government-wide statements — they are not excluded.
explanations.b: The governmental activities surplus of $500,000 cannot be compared to the business-type surplus without netting program revenues against expenses first. Additionally, the $3,000,000 without deducting operating expenses is not a meaningful surplus figure.
explanations.c: Depreciation IS recognized in government-wide financial statements (full accrual basis) — this is one of the key differences between government-wide statements and governmental fund statements. Fund statements do not recognize depreciation (capital assets are recorded as expenditures when acquired); government-wide statements recognize the asset, capitalize it, and depreciate it over its useful life. The $400,000 depreciation is properly included as an expense in the business-type activities analysis.
explanations.d: Government-wide statement of activities analysis: Governmental activities (general government): Program revenues and general revenues: Property taxes and other general revenues = $8,000,000; General government expenses = $7,500,000; Change in net position — governmental activities = $8,000,000 − $7,500,000 = $500,000 increase. Business-type activities (water utility): Operating revenues (charges for services): $3,000,000; Operating expenses: $2,200,000; Depreciation: $400,000; Change in net position — business-type activities = $3,000,000 − $2,200,000 − $400,000 = $400,000 increase. Total government-wide change in net position: $500,000 + $400,000 = $900,000 increase. The government-wide statement presents BOTH governmental activities and business-type activities with a total column. Enterprise funds ARE included in government-wide statements as business-type activities — they convert from their proprietary fund basis (already full accrual) without significant adjustment.

questions.name: State and Local Governments
questions.keyword: Governmental fund financial statements — fund types (general, special revenue, capital projects, debt service, permanent), balance sheet, statement of revenues/expenditures/changes in fund balances
questions.text: Which type of governmental fund is used to account for the accumulation of resources for, and the payment of, long-term debt principal and interest?

answers.text: Debt service fund — accounts for the accumulation of resources for and the payment of general long-term debt principal and interest
Special revenue fund — accounts for revenues from specific sources restricted for specified purposes
Capital projects fund — accounts for the acquisition and construction of major capital assets
Permanent fund — accounts for resources that are legally restricted so that only earnings may be used

explanations.a: Debt service funds accumulate resources needed to pay principal and interest on general long-term debt of the governmental reporting entity. Resources are transferred from the general fund or special revenue funds to the debt service fund; the fund then makes required principal and interest payments to bondholders on the scheduled due dates.
explanations.b: Special revenue funds account for proceeds of specific revenue sources (e.g., federal grants, dedicated taxes) that are restricted or committed to expenditure for specified purposes other than debt service or capital projects. They do not account for debt repayment.
explanations.c: Capital projects funds account for the acquisition or construction of major capital facilities (e.g., building a new municipal court, constructing a road). Capital project funds may receive bond proceeds and spend them on construction but do not make ongoing debt service payments.
explanations.d: Permanent funds account for resources that are legally restricted so that only EARNINGS (not principal) may be used for purposes that support the reporting government's programs. Examples: cemetery perpetual care funds, library endowments. Principal is preserved; only investment earnings are expended.

questions.name: State and Local Governments
questions.keyword: Governmental fund financial statements — fund types (general, special revenue, capital projects, debt service, permanent), balance sheet, statement of revenues/expenditures/changes in fund balances
questions.text: A county's general fund levies property taxes of $5,000,000 for the current year. By year-end, $4,700,000 has been collected and $200,000 is expected to be collected within 60 days after year-end. The remaining $100,000 is expected to be collected over the following 18 months. Under modified accrual accounting, how much property tax revenue does the general fund recognize?

answers.text: $5,000,000 — all levied taxes are revenue because the tax lien creates a legally enforceable receivable
$4,900,000 — taxes that are measurable and available (collected or collectible within 60 days after year-end) are recognized as revenue; the remaining $100,000 is deferred
$4,700,000 — only cash collected during the year is recognized under governmental fund accounting
$4,800,000 — only 96% of taxes levied are recognized, based on the collection rate

explanations.a: Under modified accrual, revenues must be both MEASURABLE (determinable amount) and AVAILABLE (collected in current period or within a short time after to be used to pay current period liabilities). The full $5,000,000 would be recognized only if the amount expected to be collected within the availability period equals the full levy.
explanations.b: Modified accrual revenue recognition for property taxes: The GASB's availability criterion: revenues are available if collected within the current period OR expected to be collected soon enough after year-end to pay current period liabilities (typically within 60 days). Recognized: Collected during year: $4,700,000; Expected within 60 days: $200,000; Total recognized revenue = $4,900,000. Deferred: $100,000 (expected in 18 months — not available) → recorded as Deferred Inflows of Resources (not revenue) on the balance sheet until it becomes available. Journal entry: Dr. Property Tax Receivable $5,000,000; Cr. Revenue — Property Taxes $4,900,000; Cr. Deferred Inflows of Resources $100,000.
explanations.c: Governmental fund accounting is not pure cash basis. The modified accrual basis recognizes revenues when measurable and AVAILABLE — including amounts expected to be collected within the availability period (typically 60 days after year-end) even if not yet received.
explanations.d: Revenue recognition is not based on a historical collection rate. The modified accrual criteria (measurable and available) govern recognition — availability specifically means expected collection within the fiscal year or within the defined period after year-end (60 days).

questions.name: State and Local Governments
questions.keyword: Governmental fund financial statements — fund types (general, special revenue, capital projects, debt service, permanent), balance sheet, statement of revenues/expenditures/changes in fund balances
questions.text: A city issues $10,000,000 of 20-year general obligation bonds at par to fund the construction of a new fire station. The proceeds are received in the capital projects fund. How are the bond proceeds recorded in the governmental fund financial statements?

answers.text: Dr. Cash $10,000,000 / Cr. Bonds Payable $10,000,000 — long-term debt is recorded in the fund that received the proceeds
Dr. Cash $10,000,000 / Cr. Revenue — Bond Proceeds $10,000,000 — proceeds are recognized as revenue in the period received
Dr. Cash $10,000,000 / Cr. Other Financing Sources — Proceeds of Long-Term Debt $10,000,000 — bond proceeds are not debt in governmental funds but rather a financing source
No entry in the fund — bond proceeds are recorded only in the government-wide statements, not in fund statements

explanations.a: Under modified accrual accounting with current financial resources measurement focus, governmental funds do NOT record long-term liabilities on their books. The fund recognizes only the current financial resources received — not the future obligation to repay the bonds. Bonds payable (a long-term liability) appears in the government-wide statement of net position, not in the governmental fund balance sheet.
explanations.b: Bond proceeds are NOT revenues — they are a financing source. Revenue represents inflows from exchange and non-exchange transactions (taxes, fines, grants, charges for services) that increase fund balance without creating future obligations. Bond proceeds create a future repayment obligation and are classified separately as 'Other Financing Sources.'
explanations.c: Under GASB governmental fund accounting: Bond proceeds are a SOURCE OF FINANCING in the current period but are not revenues (no service has been provided, no tax has been levied) and not liabilities in the fund (governmental funds don't carry long-term debt). The entry in the capital projects fund: Dr. Cash $10,000,000 / Cr. Other Financing Sources — Proceeds of Bonds $10,000,000. The $10,000,000 appears as 'Other Financing Sources' in the statement of revenues, expenditures, and changes in fund balances (below the 'Expenditures' section, after the 'Excess/(Deficiency) of Revenues over Expenditures' subtotal). The corresponding $10,000,000 Bonds Payable appears in the government-wide statement of net position, NOT in the capital projects fund balance sheet.
explanations.d: Bond proceeds are recorded in the FUND that received the cash — the capital projects fund. Entries in the fund financial statements and the government-wide statements coexist; the government-wide statements consolidate and convert the fund information using adjustment entries (e.g., capitalizing the fire station, recording bonds payable).

questions.name: State and Local Governments
questions.keyword: Governmental fund financial statements — fund types (general, special revenue, capital projects, debt service, permanent), balance sheet, statement of revenues/expenditures/changes in fund balances
questions.text: A governmental entity's general fund balance sheet at December 31 shows fund balance of $2,400,000. The government-wide statement of net position shows governmental activities net position of $18,500,000. Identify which reconciling items explain the difference and the typical reconciling items between fund balance and governmental activities net position.

answers.text: No reconciliation is needed — fund balance and net position are different names for the same concept
The difference represents government-wide revenues not yet collected — fund balance excludes receivables, but net position includes all accrued revenues
The reconciliation is irrelevant — government-wide statements are a separate reporting model from fund statements and are not mathematically related

The difference ($16,100,000) is explained by long-term assets and liabilities not reported in funds: capital assets (net of accumulated depreciation) increase net position; long-term liabilities (bonds payable, pension obligations) decrease net position; deferred outflows/inflows of resources adjust both; internal service fund balances may be included

explanations.a: Fund balance and net position are NOT the same concept. Fund balance is a current financial resources measure (governmental funds, modified accrual basis); net position is an economic resources measure (government-wide, full accrual basis). The difference can be tens or hundreds of millions of dollars for large governments.
explanations.b: Revenue timing differences are ONE of many reconciling items, but the $16,100,000 difference is primarily driven by capital assets and long-term liabilities — which create much larger differences than revenue accrual timing.
explanations.c: Government-wide statements are specifically designed to convert fund-level data to the economic resources basis using well-defined conversion entries. They ARE mathematically related to fund statements through the reconciliation schedule, which is a required part of the ACFR.
explanations.d: Typical reconciling items from fund balance to governmental activities net position (required by GASB 34): (1) Capital assets: governmental funds expense capital asset acquisitions as 'capital outlay expenditures' — the assets are not on the fund balance sheet. Government-wide statements capitalize and depreciate them. Adds net capital assets to convert to net position; (2) Long-term liabilities: governmental funds don't carry long-term debt. Government-wide statements recognize all outstanding long-term debt (bonds, leases, OPEB, pensions). Subtracts outstanding long-term liabilities; (3) Deferred outflows/inflows of resources: pension-related deferred items, bond premium/discount adjustments appear in government-wide but not in funds; (4) Internal service fund activity: if the government uses internal service funds, their net position may be added to governmental activities; (5) Revenue timing differences: accrual vs. modified accrual recognition timing (some revenues measurable but not available in funds become recognized earlier in government-wide statements). The GASB 34 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) includes reconciliation schedules that detail each category of difference — these are required supplementary information.

questions.keyword: Proprietary fund financial statements — enterprise and internal service funds, economic resources/accrual basis, statement of net position, statement of cash flows
questions.text: A city's water utility is reported in an enterprise fund. A new staff accountant asks which measurement focus and basis of accounting apply to proprietary fund financial statements. Which is correct?

answers.text: The economic resources measurement focus and the accrual basis of accounting, the same as in the government-wide financial statements
The current financial resources measurement focus and the modified accrual basis of accounting
The cash basis of accounting with no measurement focus
The budgetary basis of accounting using encumbrance recognition

explanations.a: Correct. Proprietary funds use the economic resources measurement focus and the accrual basis, consistent with the government-wide statements.
explanations.b: Incorrect. That basis applies to governmental funds, not proprietary funds.
explanations.c: Incorrect. GASB does not permit a pure cash basis for proprietary fund reporting.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Encumbrance/budgetary accounting relates to governmental funds, not proprietary fund GAAP statements.

questions.text: A finance director is preparing the proprietary fund financial statements for the annual comprehensive financial report. Which set of basic financial statements is required for proprietary funds?

answers.text: Only a balance sheet and a statement of revenues, expenditures, and changes in fund balances
A statement of net position; a statement of revenues, expenses, and changes in fund net position; and a statement of cash flows
A statement of activities and a statement of net position only
A statement of fiduciary net position and a statement of changes in fiduciary net position

explanations.a: Incorrect. That set is the governmental fund presentation.
explanations.b: Correct. Those three statements constitute the required proprietary fund financial statements.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The statement of activities is a government-wide statement, not a proprietary fund statement.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Those are the fiduciary fund statements.

questions.text: A city prepares the proprietary fund statement of cash flows under GASB and must classify cash received from a capital grant used to construct a utility plant. In which category should that cash inflow be reported?

answers.text: Cash flows from operating activities
Cash flows from investing activities
Cash flows from capital and related financing activities
Cash flows from noncapital financing activities

explanations.a: Incorrect. Capital grant proceeds are financing, not operating, inflows.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Investing activities relate to investments and loans, not capital grant receipts.
explanations.c: Correct. Grants restricted for acquiring or constructing capital assets are reported as capital and related financing activities.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The grant is tied to capital asset construction, so it is capital and related financing.

questions.text: A government operates a central motor pool as an internal service fund that predominantly serves governmental departments. The accountant must determine how the internal service fund is presented in the government-wide statement of net position. Which treatment is appropriate?

answers.text: It is reported only in the fiduciary fund statements and excluded from the government-wide statements
It is reported as a discretely presented component unit
It is eliminated entirely and never appears in any financial statement
It is reported in the proprietary fund statements but generally consolidated into governmental activities in the government-wide statements when it predominantly serves governmental departments

explanations.a: Incorrect. Internal service funds are proprietary, not fiduciary, and are included in the government-wide statements.
explanations.b: Incorrect. An internal service fund is part of the primary government, not a component unit.
explanations.c: Incorrect. It appears in the proprietary fund statements and within governmental activities.
explanations.d: Correct. Internal service fund balances are reported as proprietary funds but folded into governmental activities at the government-wide level when governmental departments are the predominant participants.

answers.text: A custodial fund
A capital projects fund
An enterprise fund
A permanent fund

explanations.a: Correct. Assets held in a purely custodial capacity that cannot finance the government's programs are reported in a custodial fund.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A capital projects fund is a governmental fund for capital acquisition, not a fiduciary fund.
explanations.c: Incorrect. An enterprise fund is a proprietary fund for business-type activities.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A permanent fund is a governmental fund whose earnings benefit the government or its citizenry.

questions.text: A city accountant is determining how its pension trust fund is presented. Which statement correctly describes fiduciary fund reporting under GASB?

answers.text: Fiduciary funds are reported only in the government-wide statement of activities
Fiduciary funds are reported in a statement of fiduciary net position and a statement of changes in fiduciary net position, and are excluded from the government-wide financial statements
Fiduciary funds use the modified accrual basis with a balance sheet like governmental funds
Fiduciary funds are combined with proprietary funds into a single statement of net position

explanations.a: Incorrect. Fiduciary activities are excluded from the government-wide statements.
explanations.b: Correct. Fiduciary funds use those two statements and are excluded from the government-wide statements.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Fiduciary funds use the economic resources focus and accrual basis.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Fiduciary funds have their own separate statements.

questions.text: A reviewer asks why pension and custodial (fiduciary) funds are excluded from a government's government-wide financial statements even though they appear in the fund statements. Which rationale is correct?

answers.text: Fiduciary resources are immaterial by definition and omitted for simplicity
Fiduciary funds use a budgetary basis incompatible with any external statement
The resources are held in a trustee or custodial capacity for parties outside the government and cannot be used to finance the government's own programs
GASB prohibits any reporting of fiduciary activities in audited financial statements

explanations.a: Incorrect. Exclusion is based on the nature of the resources, not materiality.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Fiduciary funds use the accrual basis, not a budgetary basis.
explanations.c: Correct. Fiduciary resources benefit external parties and cannot support the government's programs, so they are excluded from the government-wide statements.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Fiduciary activities are reported in the fiduciary fund statements.

questions.text: A government receives a trust under which only investment earnings, not principal, may be spent, and the earnings benefit specific private individuals rather than the government's own programs or citizenry. How should the trust be classified under GASB?

answers.text: A permanent fund (a governmental fund), because only earnings may be spent
A special revenue fund, because the resources are restricted
An enterprise fund, because the trust generates investment earnings
A private-purpose trust fund (a fiduciary fund), because the trust benefits specific external private parties

explanations.a: Incorrect. A permanent fund applies when earnings benefit the government or its citizenry, not specific private parties.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A special revenue fund is a governmental fund for restricted operating resources of the government itself.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Generating earnings does not make a trust a business-type enterprise fund.
explanations.d: Correct. A trust benefiting specific external private parties is a private-purpose trust fund, a fiduciary fund.

questions.text: A government converts its governmental fund financial statements to the governmental activities column of the government-wide statements. Which conversion is required?

answers.text: Convert from the current financial resources focus and modified accrual basis to the economic resources focus and accrual basis
Convert from the accrual basis to the cash basis of accounting
No conversion is required because both use the same measurement focus and basis
Convert from the budgetary basis to the modified accrual basis

explanations.a: Correct. Governmental funds (modified accrual) are converted to the economic resources focus and accrual basis for governmental activities.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Neither presentation uses the cash basis.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The two presentations use different measurement focuses and bases.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The conversion is from modified accrual to full accrual, not from a budgetary basis.

questions.text: In reconciling the net change in governmental fund balances to the change in net position of governmental activities, a government recorded $500,000 of capital outlay expenditures and $120,000 of related depreciation during the year. What is the net reconciling effect of these two items?

answers.text: Subtract both the $500,000 and the $120,000 from the change in fund balances
Add back the $500,000 capital outlay (capitalized as assets) and subtract the $120,000 depreciation, a net increase of $380,000
Add both the $500,000 and the $120,000 to the change in fund balances
No reconciliation is needed because both items are treated identically under both bases

explanations.a: Incorrect. Capital outlay is added back, not subtracted.
explanations.b: Correct. Capital outlay is capitalized (added back) and depreciation is recognized (subtracted), netting to a $380,000 increase.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Depreciation reduces, not increases, the change in net position.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Capital outlay and depreciation are treated differently under modified accrual versus accrual.

questions.text: During the year a government issued $1,000,000 of general obligation bonds (recorded as an other financing source in the funds) and repaid $200,000 of bond principal (recorded as an expenditure). What is the net effect on the reconciliation from change in fund balances to change in net position?

answers.text: Add the $1,000,000 proceeds and subtract the $200,000 repayment
Make no adjustment because bond transactions affect both bases identically
Subtract the $1,000,000 proceeds (a long-term liability, not revenue) and add back the $200,000 principal repayment (reduces the liability, not an expense), a net decrease of $800,000
Subtract both the $1,000,000 and the $200,000

explanations.a: Incorrect. Proceeds are not revenue under accrual; this reverses the correct treatment.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Bond transactions are treated differently under the two bases.
explanations.c: Correct. Bond proceeds are a liability (subtracted) and principal repayment reduces a liability (added back), netting to an $800,000 decrease.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The principal repayment is added back, not subtracted.

questions.name: State and Local Governments
questions.keyword: Deriving government-wide statements and reconciliation — converting governmental funds (modified accrual) to governmental activities (accrual); reconciling fund balances to net position
questions.text: An auditor reviews a government's reconciliation of total governmental fund balances to net position of governmental activities. Which combination of adjustments is conceptually correct?

answers.text: Subtract capital assets and add general long-term liabilities because the government-wide statements use modified accrual
Make no adjustments because fund balance always equals net position of governmental activities
Add only cash and subtract only accounts payable, ignoring capital assets and long-term debt
Add capital assets net of accumulated depreciation, subtract general long-term liabilities, and adjust for other items (e.g., deferred inflows/outflows) not reported in the governmental funds

explanations.a: Incorrect. The government-wide statements use accrual, and this reverses the adjustments.
explanations.b: Incorrect. They differ because of capital assets and long-term liabilities.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The major reconciling items are capital assets and long-term liabilities.
explanations.d: Correct. Net position adds capitalized assets, removes long-term liabilities, and reflects other accrual items absent from the funds.

questions.text: A government reports net position in its government-wide statement of net position. Which three components make up net position under GASB?

answers.text: Net investment in capital assets; restricted; and unrestricted
Assigned; committed; and unassigned
Contributed capital; retained earnings; and reserves
Nonspendable; restricted; and unreserved

explanations.a: Correct. GASB net position comprises net investment in capital assets, restricted, and unrestricted.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Those are governmental fund balance classifications, not net position components.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Those are not GASB net position components.
explanations.d: Incorrect. 'Nonspendable' and 'unreserved' are fund balance terms, not net position components.

questions.text: A city has general fund resources that cannot be spent because they exist as inventory and prepaid items. In the governmental funds balance sheet, how should these amounts be classified within fund balance?

answers.text: Unassigned fund balance
Nonspendable fund balance
Restricted fund balance
Net investment in capital assets

explanations.a: Incorrect. Unassigned is the residual classification in the general fund, not for nonspendable items.
explanations.b: Correct. Amounts not in spendable form, such as inventory and prepaids, are nonspendable fund balance.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Restricted reflects externally enforceable limitations, not the spendable form of the asset.
explanations.d: Incorrect. That is a government-wide net position component, not a fund balance classification.

questions.text: A government levies property taxes for the calendar year and expects some collections more than 60 days after year end. For the governmental fund statements under modified accrual, when should property tax revenue be recognized?

answers.text: Entirely when levied, regardless of collection timing, because property taxes are an exchange transaction
Only when cash is ultimately collected, even years later

When measurable and available — collected within the period or soon enough after (commonly within 60 days) to pay current liabilities; amounts not available are reported as deferred inflows of resources
Never in the fund statements; property taxes appear only in the fiduciary funds

explanations.a: Incorrect. Property taxes are an imposed nonexchange transaction, and modified accrual applies an availability criterion.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Modified accrual is not the cash basis; the availability criterion governs.
explanations.c: Correct. Modified accrual recognizes revenue when measurable and available, deferring amounts not available.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Property taxes are general government revenue, not fiduciary.

questions.text: A government assesses a fine (an imposed nonexchange transaction) and collects sales taxes (derived tax revenue) near year end. How should each be recognized in the government-wide (accrual) statements?

answers.text: Both are recognized only when cash is received, even in the government-wide statements
Neither is recognized in the government-wide statements because tax revenues appear only in fund statements
Both must be deferred until the subsequent fiscal year regardless of when the claim or exchange arises
Derived tax revenue (sales tax) is recognized when the underlying exchange occurs, and imposed nonexchange revenue (fines) when an enforceable legal claim arises, both on the accrual basis

explanations.a: Incorrect. The government-wide statements use accrual, not cash, recognition.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Tax revenues are recognized in the government-wide statements.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Recognition follows the exchange or enforceable claim, not an automatic deferral.
explanations.d: Correct. Under accrual, derived taxes are recognized with the underlying exchange and imposed nonexchange revenue when the enforceable claim arises.
